utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber wishes to explain that it hasn't been possible to start the proceedings for the afternoon as scheduled at 1415 hours because the sittings for the morning sessions go beyond 1345, so it takes time to clear the courtroom. That's why we're not able to sit on time. So until that improves, I'm afraid we may be running a little late. The Trial Chamber wants to explain to the witness that it is no longer necessary for the witness to produce any photographs of his house or any other house where he used to live at the material time, because the Trial Chamber did get a full explanation through their questions and through the explanations given by the witness using the photograph D16/4. So the witness should not be concerned with bringing any other photographs. The matter has been cleared. So the cross-examination can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. This also helps in my cross-examination, so I won't have to go back to this topic again. Cross-examined by Mr. Lazarevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Dagovic. I will continue where we left off yesterday. While I was going over the transcript, I've noticed some mistakes which occurred primarily in the translation of a question that I put to you. So I would like to clarify that by asking this question of you again. It's a question relating to the time up until the 4th Detachment existed. So on the transcript on page 5835, line 5, I saw that it was in the transcript that I asked you, "Do you know of the fact that the 4th Detachment ceased to exist on the 12th of May, 1992, when it joined -- became part of the units of the army of Republika Srpska." And I asked you whether it had become the 5th Battalion of the army of Republika Srpska. And I had asked you whether this was possible. So now, now that you see how I've formulated this question, I wanted to ask you whether that was the time that the 5th Battalion of the army of Republika Srpska came into being and if this is something that you know.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the same people were in the town and in the camp. What the name of that army was or the battalion, I don't know, or when this change took place, I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I just wanted to correct this technical question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... respecting our rules to pause, please, after the witness has given an answer, because the interpreter has to complete the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I'll have this in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, I also noticed some other things while I was carefully reading the transcript of yesterday's session. This concerns the moment when, according to your testimony, you saw Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tadic for the first time. Yesterday you stated, transcript page 5823, lines 12 and 13, that you saw them practically -- the two of them together for the first time some three or four metres away. And will now quote the transcript in English and you will get a translation. [In English] "Four metres, the street and my yard, and that's when I saw them." [Interpretation] So that means you practically saw them from the gate of your courtyard as they were standing with the gun pointed towards your house, the barrel. That was the first time that you saw Tadic and Zaric; is this true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree with that. I said that I saw him for the first time from the window of my house, so not from the gate of my house, that was the second time. So let's not mix those two things up. The first time I saw them was from the window of my house, and it was more than 3 or 4 metres away. It was a distance of some 10 metres, if I'm not mistaken. And then the second time, it was like you said, from 3 to 4 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you that precisely in order to clarify things that are already in the transcript. The question was: When you first saw it, that was the question, and what I read out to you, what I quoted, was your answer, the way it was recorded in the transcript. So now I'm talking about Zaric and Tadic. So did you see them when the tank was already standing in front of your house and they were standing on the caterpillar of the tank, or did you see them before that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm giving you the same answer again. That was the second time. We clarified this yesterday. But if you remember yesterday, you asked me whether the barrel was already turned towards the house for the first time. And I said no, because that was when they were still moving. Once they stopped in front of my house, that was the second time, not the first time, but the second time, then it was from 3 or 4 metres away, the second time. I don't know what's in the transcript, but I know what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this is precisely what we are trying to clarify so that the transcript would reflect what you actually said. So in relation to the first time that you saw them, could you please tell me whether they were walking or going behind the tank, next to the tank, in front of the tank. Where were they?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you listen to me carefully, I responded in my previous answer. Next to the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And one more clarification, please, for the transcript. I carefully listened to what you said. So when you got to the gate of your yard, the barrel was already turned, is that true, towards your house?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, on that occasion how was Mr. Zaric dressed? What kind of a uniform was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric had a camouflage uniform, which was different from the uniforms of regular soldiers. As opposed to uniforms of regular soldiers, he was wearing an officer's camouflage uniform, which was of a lighter shade of green than the normal uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The uniform, the camouflage uniform of a lighter shade of green, you also mentioned during the examination-in-chief by the Prosecution when you were talking about Mr. Zaric. So on that occasion, when he was collecting the weapons, was he wearing the same uniform that you were describing then?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He always had the same uniform. Sometimes he also had a officer's bag with him, and sometimes I also saw that he was carrying an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I was going to ask you now. We are still now with the situation of the collection of weapons, and this is precisely what I wanted to ask you, whether Mr. Zaric had any weapons on that occasion. So I'm talking about this event of the collection of weapons.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Automatic weapon. Can you tell us what kind of an automatic weapon?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was able to see, it was either a Kalashnikov or a Zastava automatic rifle. But he did have an automatic weapon in his hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to go back -- excuse me, I will do that later. I have just one more question relating to this issue, and then we will go on to another topic. After you handed over your pistol which was in the cellar of your house, the soldiers left; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the yard, and then later I went inside the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the yard?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how long, but long enough to see the direction that they left in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to present to you now a few specific details from your statement that you provided on the 9th of November before this Tribunal. It's on page 3915. I will read this in English. And it states there, as follows: [In English] "... going along the street, and Mr. Simo Zaric and Mr. Miroslav Tadic were standing on this tank." [Interpretation] You told us today that they were walking next to the tank. So which of these two is true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you're trying to confuse me or you don't understand. I said yesterday -- and let's go back to that -- that the first time that they were walking, they were not on the tank, because the tank was moving. And the second time that I saw them standing on the tank -- well, so please read that to the end and then ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, I am reading in English what it states in the transcript from the 9th of November, 2001, where it state that the tank was moving and that they were standing on it. And in view of their age and the situation, it didn't seem logical to me for them to be standing on the tank as the tank was moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That question is argumentative. Could they rephrase the question, please. He's making an argument that's not a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, it states here in the transcript that the tank was moving and that Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tadic were standing on it; is this true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As I told you, I abide by what I have said yesterday and today. So perhaps if this was a mistake in the writing, just like the ones that you pointed out, well, I don't know. I don't know what I said. As long as the tank was moving, they couldn't have been standing on its caterpillars. Even a small child knows that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were not standing on the tank that was moving. Can we conclude that now?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not standing on the moving tank. But once it stopped, they were standing on it then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say that they were standing on the caterpillars of the tank?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, you talked about some shelling and how your relative was killed by a shell, and you stated that while you were questioned by my colleague, Mr. Krgovic. Are you familiar with the fact that there was an attack by the Croatian Air Force against Samac and that bombs were dropped on the town of Samac on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that. And if you remember, and if you've read that, and I stated that yesterday they were targeting the post office, and they hit a private house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we didn't clarify that precisely at that time. Now we're speaking about an attack by the Air Force when bombs were dropped from the air. So are we talking about the same event?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say, "the Air Force," I wouldn't call it that, because it was an agricultural airplane. So it was one airplane and not the Air Force. But just one agricultural airplane.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that plane?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the plane at that time, since I was in the camp, but I heard the noise it was making, its sound. And this sound is different from the sound of a fighter plane.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "an Air Force plane," you mean a jet -- you mean the sound of a jet plane; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I'm not thinking of a jet plane, I'm thinking of a military plane. So it would not be only -- or just a jet plane. It would also be a bomber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this happened, could you please tell me what the bombs that were dropped then, what did they hit in Samac, which targets?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about one target because it happened to be in my street, just across from my house, and it hit the house of Jusuf Arnautovic. And if other bombs fell, I don't know. But I know that there was talks that they were trying to hit the post office and the waterworks, and they must have missed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is as much as you know about this?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is as much as I know. But I know this about the house of Arnautovic because I also have photographs of that event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, in your statement, you spoke about the looting of the pizzeria of the Bicic brothers, and you said this because you were involved with this against your will, and you said that police officers, as well as occasionally soldiers from the 4th Detachment, participated in this. And this is on page 3957 of the transcript. So now I'm interested whether you could precisely state which soldiers of the 4th Detachment took part in this. Could you tell us their names, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can tell you that amongst others - and I will tell you their nicknames - Tubonje, i.e. Tubonjic. Also Neven, the son of Boris Markovic was there. I don't know his last name. I've forgotten it. This is his younger son, and I think his name is Neven. But I'm sure it was his younger son, he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that based on that, we would be able to know which persons you are talking about. During the questioning yesterday by Mr. Krgovic, you said that even before the outbreak of the conflict, you used to see soldiers of the 4th Detachment on patrol in uniform. Could you please tell me whether you saw Simo Zaric before this event while he was patrolling in uniform in Samac. And we're talking about the period before the 16th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him in uniform, but I don't know if he was on patrol or whether he was just moving around. But I know that he was in uniform. And if I may be allowed to add, I can provide photographs of this, dated photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me the exact occasions that you saw him before the 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it happened on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you remember any such occasions? And if you can remember, could you please tell us so.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't go into the dates, but I can obtain photographs and then you will be able to see the dates on these photographs. But on several occasions during the war, i.e., immediately prior to the outbreak of hostilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So right now you are not able to give us a specific date.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't commit to a specific date, but I did see him several days, two, three, four, five days. And it was not only Simo Zaric. There were several more soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, you never saw any kind of official list of the members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any such list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never saw them lined up at all, the entire 4th Detachment all lined up?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them like that. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to move to a different topic now, and I assume this topic is more unpleasant for you, because it's the period of your -- when you were detained in the MUP building. So we will just go over that briefly, and we won't go into too much detail. You spent about five months there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time, you were taken on labour duty in Samac, in several villages in the outskirts of Samac, and then also for a while, you worked in a garage.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us - and I assume that you cannot say that in every case, but on average - when were you usually taken for this work duty? When did this take place?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This wasn't only in the morning. Sometimes it was for a half day, it was in the morning, sometimes it was in the evening. It depends. I cannot give you a specific time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you tell me most frequently when you were taken out. Or perhaps there is no particular rule about that.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no sense to it nor any kind of rule, so it wasn't any kind of set practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those five months, you spent some of that time in hospital, receiving treatment for your injuries; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not it. I spent about six months in the camp. And out of that, I was in the camp for five months and I was in the hospital for one month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay in the camp, in the MUP building where the garages were, did you used to see this person Tubonjic there, whom you said had taken part in the robbery of the Bicic pizzeria? Is that where you saw him?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did see him at that time, and he had transferred from the 4th Detachment to the police forces. So before that, he was in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did he formally transfer from the 4th Detachment to the police? What date was that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He wasn't kind enough to tell me that, and I wasn't interested either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague now provided me with information about this other man which took part in the robbery of the Bicic pizzeria. I've been told that his name is Nino Markovic. Is that the person?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, right, Nino Markovic, the younger son of Borislav Markovic, nicknamed Smudj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, now that we've identified that person --

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- did you also see him?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel repeat the last part of his question?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did happen to see him because he was driving my car which was confiscated by the army, the paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There was one part where the interpreter didn't catch the end of your question, if you look at the end of the transcript in line 13, I think, where you said, "Well, now that we've identified that person --" you did say something else which the interpreters didn't catch. So they ask that you repeat your sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. We seem to have overlapped again with the interpreters. I said, "We finally now identified that person." Is that Nino Markovic, is that that same person?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you used to see him in the MUP building as well at that time during your period there at the camp. And you said that you remembered him because he used to drive your car around.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him just like I saw all the other members of the 4th Detachment who used to come to the police station probably in order to abuse the people who were being kept there or the like. And I can also name them, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The difference between -- you differentiate between a police officer and a soldier on the basis of the uniform that they wore, I assume.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only on that basis, but also we were guarded by the police officers and we were beaten by the soldiers together with the police officers. Meaning, if the soldiers hadn't had a good day on the front or somebody was killed, then they would come and beat us, and they would take it out on us, or when they were having meetings with the chief of police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, I have very few questions left for you. In your testimony, you said that the soldiers greeted Simo Zaric with respect. It's on page 3991 of the transcript. When you say "with respect," do you mean a military salute with their hand touching their heads? Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said "with respect," that's what I meant, regardless of whether it was a handshake of a military salute. I can't remember exactly what it looked like. But I remember that they respected him, and that's how they treated him when they greeted him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I may have got the wrong impression. You know, this is being interpreted into English, and then we interpret it back into our language. So I understood you to mean a military salute, standing at attention and raising one's hand to one's head. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among other things, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You served in the JNA. You spent quite a lot of time there. And I trust that you are familiar with the rules of the service, as they existed at the time when you were there. Do you know what I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But these soldiers had nothing to do with the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put the following question to you: In the rules of the service, were soldiers of a lower rank duty-bound to give a military salute to a higher-ranking soldier, standing at attention and raising their hand to their head?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But that was not former army, in the army of Republika Srpska, I don't know how it was. Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, I think I am not revealing anything new when I say that this way of saluting is common to all the armies in the world, everywhere, and that it's not at all unusual for a lower-ranking soldier to greet a higher-ranking one with a military salute.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think we're getting off track here on relevance, if we could just move on. We're just getting off track. The witness previously indicated that there was some saluting. He remembered some sort of respect. He couldn't recall the different actions, whether it was shaking hands, standing at attention out of respect. We're moving way off track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. Counsel, I hope you have understood what Mr. Weiner is objecting to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I won't insist on this line of examination. I mean, I was talking about fact of some common knowledge about how military officers salute each other, and that was basically what I was thinking. Just a few more questions in regard to one topic, and I will finish with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me put just one more question to you in connection with something you mentioned in your testimony before this Tribunal, and you mentioned it again today. This is the bag that Mr. Zaric carried on his right shoulder. You said earlier that you thought it contained important documents. Is that correct? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. But I said also that I thought they were important documents because he was going to see the chief of police. So I'm sure he wasn't carrying biscuits to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He never opened the bag in front of you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the bag open by accident? Maybe something fell out that you could see?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He could have been carrying a newspaper, a notebook, his breakfast; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't actually know what was in the bag, do you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well, but it seems that you don't know. I said an officer's bag. When I said "an officer's bag," I meant a bag for documents. It's three, four, maybe five centimetres thick, and about 25 or 30 centimetres long at the most. So neither a newspaper nor his breakfast nor cakes or biscuits could fit in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, I will ask you again -- and this is really my last question. But you can only assume what was in the bag.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In view of the fact that I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, for one second I would like to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With the permission of the Honourable Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- I would like my client to show his bag to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. You should collect the bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And show it to the witness, because we are not allowing direct dealings between the witness and the accused person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is why I asked for permission. Yes, thank you. Your Honours, I would kindly ask for instruction at this moment. I hope that I won't have to tender this bag into evidence because it would cause a serious problem with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because -- especially that we don't wish to know the contents. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because I was going to find out from you the status of the bag. How would you describe -- Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think he first has to ask the witness if this is the bag or if he recognises the bag. Otherwise we can't have Mr. Zaric coming to testify to the bag at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, is this the bag?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bag you talked about, was it approximately this size?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe the height was the same or a little less, but not the width, not the depth. If you read the transcript carefully, you will see that I told you the width, the height, and the depth. And the height was different. I would not call this bag an officer's bag. I never saw a bag like this. This looks like the kind of bag you take on vacation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we be precise, then. Was that an officer's bag of the former JNA, the bag that you saw Mr. Zaric carrying?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the sort of bag carried by officers in the former JNA. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just add, to avoid another error, I don't know whether there were other officers' bags. I'm not saying that this is not an officer's bag. It's not the bag that he carried. Yes, that's what I meant. I didn't mean this particular bag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, before you take back the bag, maybe we can have a description of the bag for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the record may reflect, I have shown to the witness a man's leather bag --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we can -- Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to add, could we photocopy it at the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Actually I was going to ask that, because I was thinking whether we should have it shown on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because then it would be contained in the record. Yes, the usher can put it on the ELMO, front and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then -- yes, turn it over. The other side, the back side. We are all agreed that it's a brown colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that we have a picture. And as soon as we get a photocopy of this, I will ask for the identification or some other number for this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think just a photograph will do, so that we don't inconvenience the owner of the bag by retaining the bag on the record. Yes, except to show that the bag showed on the ELMO is not, according to the witness, the bag that he saw the accused carrying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's clear enough. And I have finished with my cross-examination of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Esad Dagovic, I just need a clarification here. The bag that you saw and which you say was an officer's bag, 3, 4, 5 centimetres thick and 25 to 35 centimetres long, what colour -- can you remember what colour it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a dark red/brown -- reddish brown, kind of burgundy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And if I could also ask you a question. Was it a leather bag or a canvas bag? Did it have a handle and a shoulder strap? Any other details that might assist us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The bag I saw here is that -- it has a plastic handle. The other bag had a leather strap. And like this bag, it could be carried over the shoulder on a strap. And it was made of leather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I have been advised by the technical people that actually if the usher goes back and stands with the bag to show it on the ELMO, they can actually take photographs of it right now so that we don't have to wait for the photographs. Maybe we can do that right away and then proceed with the cross-examination. I hope it's securely closed so we don't see the contents. I hope we can follow the same language with the technical booth. Can you phone them and give the instructions if we need to -- the usher needs to be told how he should place the bag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I take it we are through?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, there is only one issue in regard to this bag. I would like that the record reflects --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Actually, that the handle of this bag is actually leather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That the what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That the handle of this bag is actually made of leather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The strap or the short --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is leather, yes, this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We can't see the handle from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please, I -- yes, I would like it to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because we've got it on record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see, it is covered with leather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Do we agree, counsel, that the handle is covered with leather? MR. DI FAZIO: May I just see the bag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, the Prosecution haven't seen the bag. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't think there's any dispute that it's leather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. I think I would totally agree with you, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, my learned colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: If I might just seek another clarification from the witness, Mr. Esad Dagovic. You saw this bag, what, some ten years ago, long ago. It's been quite a time now -- quite a long time. Well, we all know that hides are tanned coloured. When you saw it, it was reddish brown. It's a kind of brown now. Would you like to comment on whether with the reflection of time, the colour may become faded as the bag gets older. So would you have any knowledge of that, because I believe you may, yourself, have been having such bags or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's possible for it to fade. But I don't think it can shrink, and I don't think it can change its Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. handle. But of course it's possible that it could fade. I agree. When I was in the army, I was a squad leader and I carried a bag of that kind. When we had exercises, and I used to use it to carry the plans for the exercises and documents, so I know very well what sort of bag it was and how it's made. When I said it had a plastic handle, I hadn't held it in my hand, I only saw it from a distance. But that bag had a leather handle which was about half a centimetre thick. And at the sides, there were two rings or hooks attaching this. So it did not look at all like this bag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Next counsel to cross-examine. Or Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more issue. After I noticed that this is going to be photographed on the ELMO, maybe we should have an ID number for the photograph that we are going to receive from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. When it comes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When it comes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, I wonder, before I start, I just have received the translation of some ten documents which are IDed with the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The ones we -- we had dealt with before, the ones that we're awaiting translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that we are waiting for. And if you want me, I can tender them at the evidence at this time, because those are just the translation. The documents are already registered. These are the D22 A/2 until D22 I/2. So these are the English translation, official translations of these documents. I have given them to the -- to my learned colleagues from the Prosecution already a couple of days ago, and with ERN numbers and all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. I think what we should do -- you can hand them over. And because some of the documents the Prosecution were not sure because of lack of translation, I think we will deal with that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that we don't waste any time with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will hand it to the usher and we will proceed with them later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, may I start with my cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Cross-examined by Mr. Zecevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, my name is Slobodan Zecevic. Tell me, Mr. Dagovic, in the course of your testimony yesterday, on page 5804 of the transcript of the 13th of February, 2002, which was yesterday, in line 9 and the subsequent lines, you said in answer to a question put by my colleague:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Q. Just mentioned Muhamed and Hasan Bicic. So I just wanted to ask you something about their families. Were they in Samac at that time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps when they left Samac, the families of Hasan and Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left immediately before the outbreak of the war. But I don't know exactly when." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember, then, that the families of Mr. Muhamed and Hasan Bicic left Samac before the war?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately before the outbreak of the war, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You should know this well, because you were employed at the Rendezvous and you saw them on a daily basis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But these are family matters. I need not know everything that went on in their families. I agree. So I only knew what went on in the pizzeria, if you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The house on Muhamed and Hasan Bicic is about 50 metres away from your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to work at the pizzeria, did you usually pass by their house?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I assume that their wives and their mother, had they been there, you would have seen them just before the war, assuming that they were there, you would have seen them, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, even when they were there, I didn't see them every day. And let me correct you. Hasan Bicic was not married; he didn't have a wife. There was only one wife, and she belonged to Muhamed Bicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you of your statement of the 8th of November, 2001. On page 3911, and that was an interview conducted by the Prosecution, in response to a question put by my learned friend:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Q. Where was the Bicic home in relation to your home?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was halfway from my house to the pizzeria, that is to say, 50 metres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you gave the Bicics the money, did you return home?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see the Bicics again later that morning?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you come to see them?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since their mother and the wives of Hasan and Muhamed Bicic, they came to my mother's for breakfast and coffee." [Interpretation] Let me remind you, you spoke here about the morning immediately after the outbreak of hostilities in Bosanski Samac, that is, the 17th of April, 1992. It follows from this that the mother and wives - that's what it says here, in the plural - of Muhamed and Hasan Bicic came to your mother's for breakfast and coffee. Tell me, sir, what is correct, what you said yesterday or what you said on Thursday, the 8th of November, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you read my first statement carefully, you will see clearly that I said that Hasan and Muhamed came to have breakfast and coffee with me, and not their wives and mother, because Hasan is not married at all. So that's absurd. I couldn't have said that. He's not married. He has a child with a woman who lives in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object at this time. Because if you look at that sentence, the sentence doesn't make sense grammatically. But the rest of the sentence, it's obvious that there are words missing in that sentence in the transcript. And too, he's taking the mean that wives came to the Bicics' house. It's -- I remember the testimony. The sentence as it is in the transcript is incorrect, and it doesn't make any sense. The sentence is "Since their mother and the wives of Hasan Bicic, they came to my mother's for breakfast and coffee," I think it should have been since they were away. But even as it stands here, it doesn't make any grammatical sense. And I think it's incorrect or wrong to try to impeach him with a sentence that doesn't make any sense. Obviously, it's a transcription error.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I respond, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking the clarification at this time. I'm not impeaching the witness. I'm just asking the clarification at this time. And I was reading exactly from the transcript. It's the page 3911, 8th November 2001. This is actually the row 10 and 11. "A. Since their mother and the wives of Hasan and Muhamed Bicic, they came to my mother's for breakfast and coffee."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have understood it to refer to the mothers and the wives of this other gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So as you say, you are seeking clarification from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You are not challenging him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. As long as he is not challenging. Because, as I said, we maintain the transcript is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because we all know sometimes there are mistake so he wants to seek clarification, as he has stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm not challenging witness at this time. It depends on his answer, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that is understood. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please. Could counsel please indicate, is it clarification of numbers of wives that we are seeking?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Clarification of the whole sentence, of the evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you were following me, my dear colleague, the first thing I asked was about the statement of the same witness given yesterday, where he said that the family of Hasan and Muhamed Bicic was away before the outbreak of hostilities. And that is the only reason I'm asking this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, not to dwell on this. You've heard what I've read out and what it states in the transcript, the official transcript. Could you please tell me which version is true? Is it true what it says in the transcript or what you told us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you said yourself, this was my questioning by the Prosecution, and we were talking about the first statement. If you take the first statement and the statement from yesterday, you will come -- you will arrive at an answer by yourself. I cannot make such a mistake. You could make such a mistake because you don't know Hasan. Mr. Pisarevic knows Hasan. Hasan wasn't married. So it's absurd to talk about two wives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you finished?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I hope you are finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Mr. Zecevic, let me warn the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel is asking questions on behalf of his client and he's also asking questions on behalf of the Trial Chamber, because we are all searching for the truth. So please do not be rude to him. Just answer the questions as he puts them. And you're not supposed to ask counsel any questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will do so. But in view of the fact that he arrogantly asked me if I had finished -- and I hadn't finished. What I said yesterday was true. And what I said the first time is also true. If there was some mistakes in the translation, this is not my fault, so I would kindly ask that such mistakes do not be ascribed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, I don't think you need to be argumentative. Just listen to the question quietly and calmly and just answer it again. If there's a mistake, just say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, I hope that you've understood the instructions from the Trial Chamber, and I would ask you kindly the following: My objective is just to clarify what is true and what is not true. I've already said twice that nobody -- or I'm not -- that I'm not trying to say that you lied. I would just like to clarify which -- what is true of these two things. Therefore, if I understood you properly, it's true what you said yesterday, that you know that the family of Hasan and Muhamed Bicic left Samac immediately prior or at some point before the 17th of April, 1992. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, you are familiar with the fact that you are on the list of the self-organised citizens of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the list from 1992 titled "The List of Self-Organised Citizens of Bosanski Samac for the Purpose of Defending the City."

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I am not familiar with that list, and I wasn't there in any capacity. If I were, I would have had weapons or been there on behalf of some organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are not aware of the fact that your name is on this list?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you hearing about this list for the first time now?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was in the camp, they mentioned some lists, I don't know, of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, of the Ustashas, the Zenga, amongst others, perhaps. They were talking about that list. But I don't know, and I've never heard of any list with that title.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that you gave three statements, I think, at the police station; is this true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two inspectors - and I'm thinking of Sarkanovic and Sadic, the ones who questioned you - did they ever mention the fact to you that you are in fact on this list?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sarkanovic did mention a list. But I don't know which list he meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that questioning, did Inspector Sarkanovic show you that list?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you never saw that list?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that list in front of you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I will show you the list in front of me. But I'm thinking of the list entitled "The List of Self-Organised Citizens in Bosanski Samac in the Capacity of the Defence of the Town"?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've never seen that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May the usher please show to the witness -- it's D14/4 ter ID. Just for the purposes, it's a list of self-organised people of Bosanski Samac, just in order that we clarify whether the witness has actually seen that or not. Oh, I'm sorry, I was advised that the transcript doesn't show it. It's D14/4 ter ID. "4," "/4."

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I turn the page? I don't see myself on this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask the questions. Just kindly place the list on the ELMO, please. Mr. Dagovic, did you ever see this list, this document, before?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The title states "The List of Self-Organised Citizens of Bosanski Samac in the Capacity of Defence of the Town"; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 5, number 155 and 156. Did you take a look?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That your same -- your first and last name, under number 156?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there is no title of the list. The title of the list is not there. So Mr. Sarkanovic could have shown me this list, but without showing me the title. But it's true that my first and last name and my address are on this list. This is something that is well known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I've understood you properly, you claim that this page 5, perhaps, is from some other document and was placed there. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But there is no title that you mentioned there. I can see my name and my address, but I don't see the name of the house. There is no number of the house. So this list doesn't say anything. It doesn't mean anything to me. Perhaps this is a list of people that should be -- who should be arrested. Perhaps that's what it is. So the name, first and last name, address.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I've heard you. But please allow me to put my question to you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 155 is the name of your brother and the name of the street that you lived in; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, will you please take this document that's on the ELMO again, and would you please look at it from page 1 until the end.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What am I supposed to be looking at? Just the names or ...? As far as I can see, mostly the lists contains the names of people who were detained, mostly those names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me -- take your time. Take a look.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There's no need. It's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, except for the first page which bears the title, is the same title on the rest of the pages, on the other pages of that same document? Would you please look.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no title or stamp either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's interested that you're saying that. Why did you say that there is no signature and no stamp either?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are trying to say that there was some kind of order there. So if that's what you are saying, then perhaps there should be some kind of official stamp or signature. Otherwise, this is something that could have been written yesterday. If I may also be permitted, may I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, can you just wait for the questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that the witness give his remark. If he wants, I am not going to, I don't know, intimidate witness in any way. I was just stopping him because of the translation. That was my only concern.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please go ahead and say what you wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, had there been a stamp -- because I did have the opportunity to see how soldiers made driver's licences and passports for themselves and would turn an illegal document into a legal one. I saw that. But even if it did have a stamp on it, still the document would mean nothing to me, because there was a state of lawlessness at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you would like to tell us, it's true, isn't it, that it was usual before the war for all official documents to bear a stamp and a signature? And I'm speaking about the time before the war. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yesterday he was made an expert on artillery. Then they were asking him -- now they're asking him if he's an expert on government documents. We have no background on -- he was a waiter at the pizzeria. I don't know if he has the qualifications to talk about government documents. We are going far beyond his expertise. I think we did yesterday, and I think we're going back into that today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, I wasn't referring to government documents. I don't know where my learned colleague got the government documents. I only said: Was it, according to his knowledge, usual that the official documents have a stamp and a signature? That's all. He, as a person who lived in the former Yugoslavia, of course is very well aware, he must have come up from time to time in possession of an official document. And actually, the witness brought it up by himself. It wasn't my line of questioning. I was just following that direction, because the witness came up with that assertion. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: By saying "official documents," are we saying government official documents? Political official documents? Party official documents? We have no background as to his expertise as to documents. In the SDA, in the SDS, the Communist Party, into all sorts of government documents. I think we got off line yesterday, getting into all sorts of issues as to multiple rocket launchers, as to airplanes, and now I think we're going off field again into various types of official documents without any background or expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner, your points are taken. And I do hope that Mr. Zecevic's questions may be of a general nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And also, as long as they are relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because sometimes a witness may bring about something, and you may want to go into it. But if it's not relevant, don't go into it, because it will obviously be ignored.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I kind of considered it was a relevant issue. Thank you. I was advised that it's the time for the break. Would you like me to break at this point or shall we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. No, no. We'll have our break. We have exceeded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we'll continue our proceedings at 16.15. MR. DI FAZIO: May I very briefly ask the Chamber a number of matters. They do affect this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: The next witness that we had intended to call has had to go back to a nearby country where he resides on account of the fact that his young daughter has been taken ill and indeed hospitalised. And I understand that he just had to simply get up and go and left today. So I wanted the Defence to understand that. We don't know what's going to happen, and I assume that they have prepared for cross-examining and hearing the evidence of that next witness, who we all know is on the list. So I just needed to alert the Chamber and the Defence to that. We'll make all inquiries, of course, to see if he can be returned and see if things can proceed smoothly on Monday. But I just don't know at this stage how things will pan out. So that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Depending on what is happening with his family, he may not be available even on Monday. MR. DI FAZIO: That's right. Now, this afternoon -- I don't know how long Mr. Zecevic is going to continue. He may be with this witness for the remainder of the day or me may finish very briefly soon after the break. If that happens, if we do finish this afternoon before the close of court sitting times, what does the Chamber want us to do? I can indicate that we could proceed immediately into submissions on the Variant A/B document. My colleague Ms. Reidy is preparing for that and will be armed and ready to go on that this afternoon if you -- if need be. Or we could proceed on Monday with submissions on that. Whatever happens, if we finish before 6.00, we won't have someone else to call into the witness box. I just wanted you to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because yesterday, we did say as soon as we finish with the present witness, including re-examination, then we will go back to Variant A and B. So that stands as unfinished business. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. So we can assume that if we finish early and we've got time left, we'll be going into Variant A and B this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, just a couple of questions about this document. Could you please tell me, since the document is in front of you, the numbers in this document, do they go in order from one side to the next, from one page to the next?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me, Mr. Dagovic, we said a while ago, if I understood you properly, that Inspector Sarkanovic asked you questions relating to this document. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said not in relation to this document, because I've never seen this list and this title. But they did mention lists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understood you properly, Inspector Sarkanovic mentioned some list, but he never showed it to you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a list, but lists, and he never showed me any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether this was during your first or second questioning in May 1992? If you remember. You looked at the statements yesterday, so perhaps --

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look at the statements -- no, I did look at the statements, but I didn't really look at the dates. I think it was -- he asked me the first time during the first statement, but he also asked me during the second time, this other one asked me during the second statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that yesterday when these two statements were presented to you - and we're talking about documents D28/3 ter and D29/3 ter - you explained to us and you read in those statements the parts that were true and the parts that were, according to you, not correct. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 5789 of yesterday's transcript, in response to a question by my learned friend: [In English]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean the whole statement or only a part of it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One part of it, the last part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us which sentence begins -- that part that's not correct begins with which sentence?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be clearer if I give you the last sentence of the part that does state what I said. I would also like to state that I did not participate in any way in the formation of the SDA, and the text that follows this sentence, I'm not familiar with." [Interpretation] Did you state that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the last sentence up until it was okay, and then all the rest that followed in my view was added on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could show D29/3 ter, please, and D29/3 be put on the ELMO, please. It's stapled together, so you cannot put the English or not? It's not a problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, could you please tell me, this is the statement that you looked at yesterday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a statement provided in Bosanski Samac on the 21st of October, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So yesterday you mentioned or you stated up until which place the statement is correct. Could you please repeat this for us again.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The correct part is more or less in the middle of the text. It states: "From the SDA," and then there's a comma. And after that, the part really, as far as I know, does not belong to my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understood you properly, the last sentence which you claim is authentic in this statement is "I would also like to state that I did not participate in any way in the formation of the SDA." Is this true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For the purposes of the Honourable Trial Chamber, it's the first sentence of the third paragraph. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think we have -- we looked at it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, thank you. Thank you. I was just trying to be helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, would you kindly read the last sentence. It's not the last sentence of the statement, because you've already read that, but the sentence before that which begins "I was told ..."

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I was told that my name was on the list of volunteers for the defence of the town, but I cannot explain how it got there." Is that the one that you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You told us yesterday, and you've repeated again now, that this part -- so the part that comes after the sentence that you've read before, which ends "in the formation of the SDA," that nothing that comes after that is true. Is that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's not what he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Yes, counsel, there's some leading here of the witness. He said that after that sentence ending with "SDA," the rest was not stated by him. It's not that it's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You see?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. [Interpretation] I apologise. I didn't mean anything bad by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the formation of the SDA, what comes after that was not stated by you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, except for the fact that I placed my signature at the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you've just read this sentence when you were told that you are on this list; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you tell us a little earlier that the inspectors really did ask you or tell you that you are on some list?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But along with that, I said that there's a third statement also which I don't see. So perhaps if you provide me with the third statement, I will get something out of that, because I signed three statements, as well as three blank statements. So I would like to perhaps have all of them, and then we will see what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, I'm not trying to present statements to you. I'm simply interested in this specific statement, and I would kindly ask you to respond to my questions. Are you, then, claiming that you stated what it says in this statement in the last sentence?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So according to you, you did not state that.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did state what comes before "SDA." Everything else that follows that, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's a fact that this was stated to you in the course of the questioning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I was about to, yes, caution counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but I really -- the situation is like this: The witness confirms that this has been told -- that he was told during the investigation that he is on some kind of list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: List, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This particular sentence exactly says: "I was told that I am on some list, but I don't know anything about it, or I cannot explain how I got to this list."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, this sentence which is in this particular statement was not stated by him. That's what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is what he says, yes. I'm just wondering what is -- what is wrong with this statement, because he confirms that this was really said to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But what you should avoid doing is to try and supplant this particular sentence into the statement which he says he agrees with, which is the preceding paragraph, up to "SDA."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours, I will withdraw my question. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dagovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I don't need the statements nor the previous document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, if I'm not mistaken, you were 23 years old in 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. Perhaps I was 21. I can't really calculate Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that. I was between 21 and 23.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born on the 28th of May, 1969.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were a lance corporal. When did you serve your military service?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999 -- in 1989. So I was fresh out of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, fresh out of the army. Where did you serve your military term?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I served my term in Karlovac, in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your specialty? What we call VES in the army.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the engineers unit. That was where I was. And I was a lance corporal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you completed your military service, you had a regular military booklet; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you completed your military duty, you reported to the appropriate military department in Samac; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Dagovic, in your military booklet, you had a wartime assignment; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I think I have the booklet at home, but I'd have to look at it. As far as I know, I did not have a military assignment in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it not your duty as a reservist if there was a war or an imminent threat of war to report to a certain place?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this has come up now three times. In each of these three times now we've objected. The issue here is whether or not they're going to try to indicate he had a duty and he violated that duty. However, as we all know, the JNA had split up, the former Yugoslavia had split up. There is no issue -- there is a serious issue of whether there was any duty. Or rather, there is no issue because there was no duty, because as the JNA as it existed in the '80s no longer existed in 1992. This line of questioning has come up three times, and each of those times, the Court has found -- has sustained our objection, saying this type of information is not allowed. You're asking him to make a legal decision as to whether Yugoslavia existed technically, then technically whether the JNA existed, and then if it did exist, whether or not he still had a duty. It really becomes a legal issue, which this Court has to make the decision. It's not the type of issue for this witness to offer an opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may respond, I was simply asking -- I appreciate what my learned colleague has explained to the Trial Chamber. But believe me, it was not my intention at all. My intention is just to ask the witness whether he's aware of his obligation as a military reservist, nothing else. I am not trying to -- to establish that he violated any of his rights or go into that area, whether he accepts JNA, BiH army or the former Yugoslavia. Just the simple answer, yes or no, whether he was aware of the fact that as a reservist he had the duty -- as a military reservist, he had a duty to, I don't know, in case of imminent war danger or wartimes, report to a certain place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that would be my last question. No other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That is before the breakup of the federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's limiting that question to prior to April of 1992 would he have had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but can you just explain that a little more. You say he had a duty. Assuming he had a duty, but what is the first step? Has he got to be called up? Did he receive a call-up notice? That must precede the duty, mustn't it? Is there any evidence that he was called up? Can you ask him if he was called up?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
