utterances.text: Of course I will but I wasn't really -- I will follow the suggestion of the Honourable Trial Chamber. I was evading, actually, that question, because I anticipated that my learned colleague will make an objection. But I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But logically I think we must try to follow this, because all you've done is refer to some booklet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: And the booklet must say something. We don't know what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. I agree, Your Honour. If I may elicit the answer to the first question and then I will ask the question which Your Honour is -- I'm grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, you heard my question.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before April 1992, as a military reservist, was it your duty to report to a certain place in case of imminent threat of war or war?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did have a duty to report there, but let me add something. Had Yugoslavia remained after 1992, I would not have gone to kill innocent women and children, even if I had been sent to prison for that. So I would not have responded to the call-up, because I saw what was happening. I saw what had happened in Slovenia and then in Croatia. But yes, I did have the call-up. You're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the duty was there, but you are telling us that due to your convictions, it would not have responded, regardless of the legal consequences; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, did you at some point before the 17th of April, 1992 receive any kind of notification, or were you called upon in a public announcement to report as a military reservist to the place where you were supposed to report? If you can remember that.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean before Bosnia and Herzegovina was established, that is, recognised? Are we talking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Witness, the counsel did give a date, and that is before 17th April, nothing more but that date. So your answer should be precisely based on that date, before 17th April, 1992, regardless of the status of which country.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I wanted to say was that Bosnia was recognised before April. That was before April. And I did receive draft notes between the time when Bosnia was recognised and April. That's why I wanted to clarify. And I did not respond to the call-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, because we are aware of both dates, does it mean that you were called up between the 6th and the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know I received the call-up after Bosnia-Herzegovina was recognised. I don't remember the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know if this was before the 17th of April? You don't remember?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was both before and after the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you received these call-up papers twice?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times, many times. After every fight, we were called up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't understand what sort of fight you are referring to. I am talking about draft notes from the Secretariat for National Defence of Bosanski Samac, from the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I spoke of this yesterday. If you understood me, when the war started, when we were in camp, first we were beaten and then people arrived telling us to go to the army. I don't know that that's exactly. I know approximately when it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, would you be so kind, you were detained on the 5th of May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the exact dates. Between the 6th of April and the 5th of May, when you were detained, did you receive draft notes? Were you called up? And if you were, do you remember how many times it was?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the dates, but it was on several occasions that I was called up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you said, you didn't want to respond to those call-ups; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in what manner were you called up? Did a courier arrive, or was there a public announcement, or did both things happen?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I was detained, there was an announcement on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An announcement for all reservists?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But because 99 per cent of the Serbs had already been mobilised, it was the others who were left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honours, would you like me to pursue this matter any more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I just wanted to know what the relevance of this line of questioning was. Was he detained on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He was detained from May 5th, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Yes. Because he detained because he did not respond to the call-up notice, or was he detained because he had a pistol at home, or because of some other thing, and then incarcerated and what happens happened? I think that is what we would like to know, why was he detained. If you know, you can suggest or put it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel, if I might add one thing to Judge Singh's question. I think if you're going to ask him all of those questions, you also have to go to the other fundamental question: Or was he incarcerated because of his ethnicity or religion? I don't think you can -- I think you've got to give him the whole gamut of possibilities if you're going to ask that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, with all due respected, I'm going to ask the question, but I don't know whether the witness will answer the questions. I don't know whether he knew why he was incarcerated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let me say this, Witness. Can you wait? Counsel, you have -- if you feel that they're not necessary for the defence of your client, then you don't have to ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm perfectly aware of that. I was just asking whether my line of questioning was enough concerning the military obligation -- the reserve military obligation, that was my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Dagovic, do you think that your incarceration on the 5th of May had anything to do with the fact that you did not respond to the announcement telling all reservists to report for military duty?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm glad you put this question to me. On the contrary. My mistake was that I reported. The list that you showed me, was perhaps a list of people who did report, because I know that people who did not report, they were not incarcerated, as opposed to us who did report and our names were found on one of these lists. So the mistake I made was to report, because this was obviously a list of citizens. Because when the so-called Republika Srpska was set up, they did not know who was still in town and who wasn't. In this way, they obtained the list. Before that, they intimidated us. They told us we would be shot. And they intimidated us to reporting. And when they did, they were provided a complete of list of the citizens who were still in town and they used it to incarcerate people, and I'm sure of this because the people who did not respond, who did not report, and who hid, were not incarcerated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that you think it is connected or not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the fact that you did not obey the announcement for military reservists?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I did report. You didn't understand me, sir. I did report to the territorial building in Samac because we were threatened with shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, please. I will try to put very clear questions to you. So you did respond to the announcement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were questioned on the 9th of November, 2001, on page 3921 you said the following to a question put by the Prosecutor: [In English]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do anything else at the Territorial Defence building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ask you, did they try and recruit you, try and mobilise you into the JNA? Did they ask you about forced labour at that point or anything else at that point?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they offered us weapons or rather to join the army of Republika Srpska. We tried, and most of other people refused, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I went to my home." [Interpretation] Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you put a question to me? I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said: Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. That's what I've been saying all along.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the issue is over the word "report," how we're all characterising the word "report." He's viewing the word "report" as reporting to the TO and I think Mr. Zecevic is referring to the word "report" as reporting to the military itself, to the JNA. And I think that's where the confusion is here. We have a word "report," and we have two different meanings of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. Zecevic can clear that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, the statement I just read back to you concerning your arrival at the Territorial Defence building, you were then reporting to a call-up from the army, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was an announcement over the radio. Who it was, I don't know. The army, probably. And I suppose it would have been somewhere else if it had been someone else, so I assume that it was the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you reported, you went there, and you did not wish to receive weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you, I did not want to take any weapons. But they put my name on a list. There weren't any questions. They just listed us, and we went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After this event, you were given a work assignment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brother also had work duties; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, this was a general duty, just like military service in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're mixing up concepts. That was not my state, so it was not my duty. I was forced to do it. Nothing was voluntary. Everything was under coercion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me put the question to you like this: Before the 6th of April, as far as you know military duty and work duty in case of war or imminent threat of war was a general obligation pertaining to all the citizens of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I'm sure it was not for all citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know if it's not for all citizens?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not logical. Some people are ill; some people are elderly, young; they don't have to do work duty. But here everybody had to go; children, the infirm, the elderly, old men and women, so this is not what you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, on the 9th of November when you were interviewed, on page 3922 you spoke of work obligation. And in line 17 in answer to a question put by my learned friend: [In English] "Q. Forced labour assignments. Give the age of the oldest -- the range of the oldest people and the youngest people.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, they were like, between 16 and 60. They asked me -- they asked for all these people to report to them. So it was between the ages of 16 and 60.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Serbs that had to work forced labour?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No." [Interpretation] Is that what you stated, sir? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Do you remember having stated this?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that has nothing to do with what we've just been talking about. Reporting and work duty --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, just answer my question, sir.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May the witness be shown the document D22 E/2 ter. Actually, right now, Your Honours, the translation of that document exists. I gave it to the registry, but I don't know whether it is appropriate that we distribute it at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, since you are going to discuss it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. D22 E/2 ter. It's a list of people engaged in the working brigade for the months April, May, June, July. I mean, just for your ... I kindly request the registrar to supply the -- oh, yes. I'm sorry. Your Honours, I'm just notified that this document is under seal, so we might not be able to put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will take care on the line of the questions. I will not ask anything concerning -- I believe I remember why it was under seal, because of the certain name of a certain witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So the English translation will be what number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: D22 E/2, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be document D22 E/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, this document bears the title "List of Workers in the Work Brigade from April to August 1992"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said a little while ago on the transcript of the 9th of November, it says that none of the Serbs were under work obligation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, none of them were, except for Pero Pita, but he was ill. He could have turned the gun on the wrong side. That's why he didn't go to the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a Serb, was he not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, either his father or his mother were Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please turn to page 2, number 44.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the name of your brother, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says that he worked for 69 days in total; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you feel that this is correct for this period of time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you'd have to ask him that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just know that he was not paid. He did not receive the remuneration that's mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was going to be my next question. Thank you for helping me. Tell me, sir, under number 92, Ilija Ivanovic, do you know this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 1, number 10, Ilija Arsic, do you know this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell by his first and last name what his ethnic background is or not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to his last name, he would be a Serb. But his first name could also be Croat. But it seems that he only had to do work obligation once. He may have been drunk and unable to go to the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at number 58, sir, please. Zivorad Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will agree that this is a typical Serbian first and last name, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But I see that he only had to work once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at the last page, page 6, number 174, please.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Vuksic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragan Vuksanovic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, Vuksanovic, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A total of 52 days.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's more than the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that he is a Serb?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I just don't know -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document has a stamp and a signature, has it not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But if I may say --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I wanted to add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness says he wanted to add something. Maybe he can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. There has been a major mistake here, since I know just like the gentlemen does that all military conscripts are obliged to report for duty in case of war. But it's absurd, then, to receive payment for such a -- an obligation. Also, the women are missing from this list, women who were on work duty. And also, since this is a regular document with a stamp and a signature, I don't see a signature here indicating that they received compensation. So this is something that would accompany such a document. So I don't see this as a valid document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So contrary to what my learned friend on the other side claims, that you were not versed in these matters, you do appear to know about these things.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you didn't ask me about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object. Is he trying to now impeach me through him, or is he trying to contradict me through him?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't pose the question. It was just the question to the witness whether he think that is he is an expert in this field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But it's the way you took it up with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I am sorry. It was just for the -- maybe it was inappropriate. I didn't mean it really as it sounded. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then, also, counsel, you should be able to look out for futility in some of the comments, in some of the excesses that witnesses say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, Mr. Dagovic, could you please tell me, this document entitled "The List of Employees Engaged in the Work Brigade," that's the title, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For a while, if I remember well -- if I remember your statement, you worked in the work brigade for a while; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did women carry out this difficult labour that the men performed in the work brigade?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And they were also humiliated while doing it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, could you please tell me the following: Yesterday when you were shown those photographs, you pointed out your house and your uncle's house; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your uncle -- your uncle's name is Sulejman Dagovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a barber by profession; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to confirm that. He's a barber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, are you aware of the fact that he also was on work duty?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He remained at his job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was in the hospital; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, do you remember whether your uncle received a salary for his work?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This is something you should have asked him, because I was in the camp at the time that he was working, so I never managed to ask him that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was in the same hospital where you received treatment, I think, from the 8th of June until the 8th of July; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I have five documents concerning the names. It's the list of the people employed at the general hospital in Bosanski Samac. These are the documents which are really similar to the ones I presented just -- I mean, before in these proceedings. It is concerning the name and the working place and the -- and the coefficient and the amount of dinners that they have been paid. Unfortunately, none of these documents I still have the translation. I would like to use them if I can have the ID number and ask the witness. It is concerning his uncle -- his uncle, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Were they handed in to the Translation Unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe seven days ago, ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. And you indicated the agency?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I indicated. But it was said that unfortunately due to the trial of Mr. Milosevic and Brdjanin and Talic, they cannot promise me anything. It may come soon but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to same way. We'll have them numbered for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would like them numbered for identification purposes, and I will really quickly go through them with the witness, if possible. Your Honours, all these documents have been -- have been disclosed to the Office of the Prosecutor, and they have their ERN numbers. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, for the assistance of other Defence counsel, not for the Chamber itself, of course, because you don't have these, these are -- can be found in volume 3 of the consolidated Defence document that the Prosecution collated and consolidated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Yes. Maybe counsel can begin with giving us the number stamped on it so that we all know which document we are discussing at a given time. Then we can give it a number for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. The first -- the first document is this list of May 1992. Could I have the identification number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Does it have an ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the ERN number is Y0005284.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's document D27/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Shall I go through all the documents so we don't lose time after this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah, the ones you wanted to discuss, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. The next document has -- I'm having problems with the ERN number. It's Y000, I assume, 52, and then the last number is 5 -- it's the same list, for June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: June 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And it's only one sheet, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is two sheets, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's the only document with two sheets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have an ID number for it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's document D28/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And the next one will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I just have to consult with my assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. The next document is -- has an ERN number Y0005288. It's the same list, for July 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have an ID number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's document D29/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next document has -- this is the information to the executive board. It bears the ERN number Y0005287, from July 23rd, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's document D30/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The last document bears the ERN number Y0005289. It is the same report, dated 12th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's document D31/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was just checking out the numbers which I have concerning the Variant A and B document, and I believe we already used the number which were given to the documents we marked just now. Because number D27/2 was a witness statement offered into evidence by my co-counsel Ms. Catharine Baen. So was 28, so was 29, 30, 31 and so on. Just in order that we clarify the transcript, I would -- I'm sorry. It's just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So this was just --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was ringing the bell, but I wasn't sure. So I just took it. Luckily I had it with me, the binder of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we reorganise the numbering, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, my last -- our last number with the reference "/2" for our client was 32/2 ter -- or 32 -- 31/2, actually, because it was admitted. D31/2 was our last number. So I assume that this other documents can go in subsequence to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that. We've already got --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I really didn't mean to cause any trouble. I just thought that it would be better that we clarify this right now, rather than later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, so that we correct the numbering.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The previous last document admitted on the 12th of February was D31/2 and D31/2 ter. I apologise. The five documents today in the same order of sequence will be from D32/2 ter ID to D36/2 ter ID. MR. DI FAZIO: Would it be safer, Your Honours, to go through each one individually, so we're all absolutely crystal clear? Because it could easily lead to problems, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the registry assistant can do that slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honours. MR. DI FAZIO: And perhaps for the assistance of counsel who have these documents, if the ERN number --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will read the ERN numbers. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would the usher be so kind to show the witness the document which bears the ERN number Y00058 -- 5284. It should be D32/2 ter. And this is this list for May 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says: "JUR general protection hospital Bosanski Samac." The title is "data about the" -- [No interpretation] Let me repeat again. "Data about the manner, conditions, and means for payment or remuneration of salaries in accordance with the determined coefficients for the months." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Beneath that, it states: "May 1992"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, could you please tell me, under number 1, it's Dr. Sisic Marko?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mirko. I apologise. It seems to me that you mentioned this doctor during your statement. He treated you; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 12, it's Sulejman Dagovic; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the continuation, it says "brico," barber?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is your uncle, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it states further along that he's in the sixth salary category, that the coefficient is 0.7; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is also a dinar amount; isn't there?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you don't know whether he received a salary or not.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know that. But I would like to add something. This is an official document, and I don't have anything against this, but I expect that you also provide me with 184 salary slips for all of these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, you consider this an official document, this document to be an official document, this specific document.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see signatures. I see a stamp. So if this is a stamp, and I also see a salary list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, by pure luck I have given to the registry the exact original of these documents. We don't have many originals, but this one is the original. Could this original be shown to the witness, please. It is the same -- that is document D32/2 ter, but it is the actual original. Maybe the -- my learned colleagues from the Prosecutor desk can check it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can also look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, this document which you just looked at and this document that you are looking at right now, they're identical, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first one is. But this is a little different, this other one, because it had a different stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a stamp?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here you can see that there's also a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you please put this original piece of paper on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, look at the screen. This stamp here underneath the date, the 22nd of April -- of June, 1992, is that a stamp?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see it's a stamp. Yes, that's right. But when I meant stamp, I meant the one on the other document. But let's not get confused here. I do see that it is a stamp, "K-2," something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's also initials above the -- above the stamp; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, could you please tell me -- my question was the following: Is this document that you see on the monitor right now and the document for which you just a little while earlier claimed to be an official document, are these two documents identical?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which sense are they not identical?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may be permitted to place the document that I had in my hands before on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dagovic, I kindly asked you when I asked you, I asked you to take the document dated the month of May 1992, not to take a different document.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I apologise. I didn't see the document was here. So this is what I thought you meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please take the document dated May 1992 and place it on the ELMO. In your opinion, could you please tell me, are these two documents which are on the screen right now identical?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, on the right-hand side at the very bottom of the document, there is some vertical writing. What does it say there? Something is typed.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Manager of the work unit, Dr. Mirko Sesic, s-c-i med dot," which is what you meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant. As far as you know, was Mr. Mirko Sesic really the manager of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's why he was not in the army, as I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you show the original -- I don't need the document D32/2 ter. But maybe for the Trial Chamber if you would like to inspect the original, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is he offering it into evidence, or are we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's already been --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is ID. This is ID. I'm not offering it into the evidence because I don't have the translation, my dear colleague. I'm just offering it for inspection. I'm sorry. May I proceed now, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, can you find the document which is the same list as this but dated June 1992?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This should be document D33/2 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... And I cannot read the ERN number. It's unreadable. It's illegible. I'm sorry, Your Honours. This is the list from June 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: D33/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have it here before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mirko Sesic is again the first on the list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please turn to page number 2 and look at number 92 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is again your uncle, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The coefficient, the amount, everything?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's all there. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think can counsel just correct the transcript. Your question was "turn to page number 2. Look at number 92." It should be 22, because the transcript has number 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It's the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yeah, it is number -- actually number 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 22, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And on page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, under number 22 in this document is the name of your uncle. And it says next to his name "barber"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Dagovic, you spent about a month in that hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me do you know Sadbera Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know her. She was fired when I was released from hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was in July?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, just after I left. I know she had another work duty after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell me, is she a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she is. That's why she was fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, your uncle was also a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He wasn't fired.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Probably because he was in poor health.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fetah Mehinagic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slavica Kurbasic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She's a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just asked you whether you knew her.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Dagovic -- well, let's go on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next document is the same list for July 1992. The ERN number is Y0005288. It should be D34/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, under number 19 is your uncle, is he not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the woman from the last document is missing, so I was right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, number 20, Muris Focakovic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next to his name, it says "worked for 13 days"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And under "post," it says mechanic on work duty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his pay class is 5, the coefficient of 1.0.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says 3.690 dinars; correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 22, Esma -- and I suppose it's Hadziabdic, do you know her?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but she was ill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She had stopped working a while before. So this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is she a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she's a Muslim by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this. Now the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The report of the hospital of Bosanski Samac to the executive board, 23rd of July, 1992. It bears the ERN number Y0005287 and should be D35/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, under number 22, Sulejman Dagovic, that's your uncle, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says "15 work days."

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the heading, if you can read it, it says: "The presence at work of the worker Jura for June 1992"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's signed by the manager of Jura, Dr. Sesic; is that correct, at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next document is the information to the -- report to the executive board of Bosanski Samac by the hospital. It bears the ERN number Y0005289 and should be D36/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it's from the 12th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, sir, you see this document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 20 is the name of your uncle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the document is entitled "Presence at work for July of workers of the work unit, July 1992"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I may add --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just finish my question.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought you had finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 21 is the name Muris Focakovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it says, "Mechanic under work obligation"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When you mentioned the lady Esma Hadziabdic you said she had stopped working.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can't remember exactly when. I'm trying to remember, but I see that there are no lists after July. After July, some refugees arrived, and all of these people lost their jobs except for my uncle who stayed at work in the same unit. And I wanted to add something, if you will allow me. In view of the fact that this is a report for July, and I see that the number of workers is 23, and there are 22 in July, so there's one missing, if that's the document that refers to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, do you know that Esma Hadziabdic is still working at the hospital in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, sir. This document was signed by the manager of the work unit, Dr. Mirko Sesic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is also a seal of the Bosanski Samac general hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, when you were interviewed in November 2001, the Prosecutor showed you some photographs. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you then testified that occasionally you cleaned the municipality building, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you also testified that you carried sandbags to the silo or around the silo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did you carry sandbags somewhere else also?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the embankment facing the hospital. That's where I carried sandbags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Dagovic, were all the important buildings in town protected by these sandbags?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this was not to protect buildings. When we were carrying them to silos, we were not doing it to protect buildings but to -- to create bunkers for soldiers from positions -- on positions from which they could shoot at people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the parapet that was erected near the hospital, was that used for soldiers to shoot behind?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were they shooting at?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of the village of Prud, a Croatian village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, you said a while ago that all the important buildings were protected with sandbags; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what you said. I didn't say it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you confirmed it was correct.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that at the silo, we were not protecting buildings but putting sandbags on the silo to create a parapet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that the general hospital in Bosanski Samac was shelled and that it was hit? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a shell landed in the courtyard of the hospital. That happened while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So apart from the parapet and the silo, you did not carry sandbags anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them around town? I'm referring to sandbags around buildings.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could see, I didn't see very many. No, in fact I didn't see any in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Dagovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown the photograph Exhibit 14A, photograph number 56.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember looking at this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's the garage and the courtyard of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember them well, especially the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in the distance behind, you can see a river.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The river Sava. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And behind it is the bank that belongs to the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, the building on the left-hand side, can you see it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was part of the municipal building where the cadastral office was?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a prefabricated building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the courtyard. I think it was prefabricated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when you went to clean the municipal building, did you go to clean that building or only the main building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just the main building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just the main building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they take someone else to clean this building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see anyone there, so I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see anyone in that part.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume it was not used, because it was opened toward -- it was not protected from fire, from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The other building was also exposed to fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did you see anyone working in that building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have only a few more questions for you, so it will take only a few minutes. Yesterday when you were examined, you stated the following: On page 5792, to a question put to you by my learned friend: [In English] "Q. And you wanted to be exchanged; right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was forced to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you whether you wanted to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not want to be exchanged and I did not want to go to the camp either." [Interpretation] That's what you said, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember in November 2001 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I completely forgot. I don't need this document any more, 14A. Thank you, Mr. Usher. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember, Mr. Dagovic, in November 2001, more precisely on the 9th of November, you talked to the Prosecutor about the same topic.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 4009, line 14, to the Prosecutor's question: [In English] "Q. You indicated that you were exchanged in early November, on November 5th. Could you tell the Court the circumstances of that exchange, please?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived and they told me I was going to be exchanged. And of course, I was happy that I would be able to leave that hell." [Interpretation] Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. There's no contradiction here. I was forced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're mixing up different things, sir.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who would want to leave their own home if they were in their right mind. Those are two different things. I did want to leave that hell, but not because I wanted to. It was because I was beaten, so I was forced to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would kindly request that the witness be instructed -- I didn't pose any question. I just asked him whether this was what he has said. He said yes and then started to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure you observed the character of the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I do understand. But I wouldn't like to, I don't know, make the witness nervous or intimidated in any respect. I just was asking simple matters concerning the transcript, verification of the transcript. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. But he has added what he thought he should add. And if you want to deal with that, you can deal with it. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to say that counsel appears to be impeaching him with a prior inconsistent statement, and it isn't inconsistent, and he was explaining why it isn't inconsistent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But it is obvious that the witness was anticipating my questions. But I have another statement I would like to present to him before the impeachment. So let me just finish this before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same date, sir, on the 9th of November last year, on page 3973, to the Prosecutor's question: [In English] "Q. Let me just jump ahead on a few questions. We will step away from Lugar for a moment. You left the hospital on what date?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hospital, around the 7th of July, a policeman named Dragan Stefanovic from the village of Crkvine came to me and he asked me or rather said to me that the Red Cross was asking whether I wanted to go for an exchange. I said yes."

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct too?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I was not exchanged, so I was tricked again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please wait for my question.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was afraid you would move away from this topic, so I wanted to say this because I feel it is very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. But do always wait for questions from counsel. If there is anything extra you want to say after counsel has finished asking you questions, you can ask for the permission from the Chamber to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, you have already explained without my asking you. But now I would like to ask you to repeat. I assume you will repeat what you have already said. So in November at one point, you said that you were glad to leave that hell. In another place you said that you were told that the Red Cross was asking for you to be exchanged and you agreed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. If the Court will allow me to explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll let you explain, but let me go on first. On the 13th of February, you said you did not want to be exchanged. Could you explain this.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, thank you. When I said I did not want to be exchanged, this was in context. It would be absurd for someone to want to leave their home and their family and be exchanged. I was happy to be leaving that hell because I had been beaten up. I had been to hospital. And when they said, "Do you want to be exchanged, to go back to camp," of course I wanted to be exchanged, to leave that hell. But nobody liked leaving their home and their family. So it was by force. You made use of this and you twisted it round to suit your purposes out of context. I was happy to leave that hell, yes. But I was not happy to be incarcerated. So I was locked up like an animal, and we don't even treat animals like that. So you used this in context -- in a context that suits you, in a legal way. But as Her Honour Judge Mumba said, I cannot wait for the question to finish because I feel I haven't answered. I've come here to tell the truth and not to be put questions to which I cannot be allowed to answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dagovic, for you exhaustive reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... with this witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, we are almost finished for today, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, is our time until 6.00 today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We may go beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Because I have other procedural matters which I want to raise, so that was my guess to know exact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Let's deal with cross-examination first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please go out for a moment, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The usher, can you escort the witness out, please. I may as well ask the interpreters, if we take a ten-minute break -- Can you escort the witness outside, please. Yes. I will ask the interpreters. If we take a ten-minute break now, can we continue?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll take a ten-minute break. --- Break taken at 5.59 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The proceeding -- we are not about to continue the proceedings as of today. We've been informed that Mr. Milan Simic is quite tired. And there's nothing we can do about that but adjourn. We shall leave it to the Prosecution to determine the sequence of their witnesses. I hope they will stick to the list. But for this particular witness, if it's possible for him to come on Monday, fine. If it's not possible, another date can be arranged. I hope Mr. Pantelic will bear with the change of timing for this particular witness, for your continued cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honours. By all means, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because the Victims and Witnesses Unit has also to arrange with his employers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I fully understand the situation. And Your Honours, I have a very brief issue to raise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- with regard to Variant A and B. This is a formal motion on behalf of all my colleagues --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Attorney Ashley Reidy is the attorney handling this. We thought this was going to be over today. She's not here today. I'd ask that this be held till Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have had little, if any, involvement in it, and I really couldn't respond to anything, in any event

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If we may add, Your Honours, I just spoke with my colleague Ms. Reidy, and she told me that it will be enough to see it in transcript. So I won't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. So what you want is to state what you want to say and then she will respond --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. She will read the transcript, and then she will be -- prepare for several days. So for the sake of efficiency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honours, our formal motion is related to the sort of subpoena to the certain number of persons which might be of -- their testimony might be of importance for this issue Variant A and B. Namely, I am thinking about the three unknown agents of AID service; let's say John Doe 1, John Doe 2, and John Doe 3. Also, I have in mind Mr. Alimanovic, who was mentioned through the testimony of Mr. O'Donnell. I don't know his first name. And also, I am thinking about the subpoena for President of -- Presidency of SDS party in Republika Srpska, Mr. Dragan Kalenic, and also the head of the SDS main office, Mr. Milovan Bjelica. Also in addition, we are mindful to call two accused persons currently under the jurisdiction of this Tribunal. Of course we have to make certain contacts with their lawyers. They are two prominent political figures. And I do believe that their testimony should be limited specifically to the issue of Variant A and B. But we shall be in a situation to give their names on Monday after the consultations with their lawyers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you -- yes. You have to discuss with these possible witnesses you intend to call, or if they are accused, you have to discuss with their lawyers and get their statements. You have to approach them and find out if they can assist your case, get their statements, before you can apply for subpoena.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was my idea, in fact. There are two ways. Maybe they can come personally here before this Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- if they want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If they agree to be invited as witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the other alternative would be sort of a statement of affidavit or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So yes, you can make those preparations. There is no need for hurrying on this issue. It can wait. We can proceed with the case when you are ready for with your witnesses. We can go back to it. There is no need for you to be in haste, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Thank you for your instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So it doesn't have to be on Monday. You can go ahead and see which witnesses you think you want to call for this particular -- for these particular documents. Make the normal arrangements. If you feel -- and you still feel you want them, that's when you can apply for subpoena.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it doesn't have to be next week. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would just like an opportunity -- once again, this is Attorney Reidy's issue to properly oppose portions of it based on when they finalise what their plan is. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If we're going to move to quash subpoenas or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's why I'm telling them that they better do it properly. There's no need for haste. And then the Prosecution, as usual, will have the opportunity to respond, like respond -- the opportunity to respond on the other witness suggested by Ms. Baen. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So no decisions are going to be taken yet. And every party will be given the opportunity they need.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Court will rise until Monday at 14.15 hours. The other point I wanted to mention was the Trial Chamber was asked as to the schedules of the sittings. The schedule -- we shall go on sitting until the week beginning the 18th of March. That week we shall not sit. Thereafter, we shall continue sitting. The written schedule will be provided as soon as Ms. Godic [phoen] comes back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of February, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
